items.review_scope: Pages 1–4 practical filing standards; dated transitional guidance, not a determination of current controlling law.
items.summary: Follow division procedures for proposed orders; the order describes erroneously filed proposed orders going to the pending queue. Separate cases require separate transactions and documents must be distinct items. Civil cover sheet and confidentiality notice are separate documents. Mail-service envelopes go to the serving court or clerk. The order states five days to correct nonconforming pending-queue submissions.

items.review_scope: Pages 1–3 general appearance, coverage and withdrawal; appendix collected, no specialized family review.
items.summary: Recognized counsel must file the initial pleading, obtain substitution or file an appearance. Coverage counsel files an appearance, subject to the same-firm exception where the firm signed the initial pleading or appearance. Civil limited-appearance termination must be filed. Sole nonsubstantive-continuance appearances have an exception. Withdrawal motions include reasons and the client’s last-known address, phone and email.

citation.label: 3.09 Standing Case Management Order in County and Circuit Civil Cases
citation.quote: The Clerk shall not accept a civil case for filing

items.review_scope: Pages 1–2 applicability and initial filing; appendix paragraph 11 conferral, pages 4–5. Other appendix deadlines collected but not substantively abstracted.
items.summary: Applies to civil actions except Rule 1.200(a) exclusions. The plaintiff signs and files the standing case-management order with the complaint and serves it on named defendants; the clerk is directed not to accept filing without it. Appendix paragraph 11 requires substantive good-faith conferral before any motion, with date/time certification; an unsuccessful-attempt statement must detail at least three attempts within the immediately preceding one-month period. Original contains track and schedule details.
